articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft casually drops fixes for 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently browsers are made of Swiss cheese now.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turned ancient routers into Office token-harvesting machines, proving once again that your dusty Linksys from 2019 is basically an open invitation to Moscow. Time to update that firmware, comrades.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower William Binney's 'turnkey totalitarian state' warning hits different when you realize we're already living in it. EFF's rallying cry to dismantle the surveillance empire before the next autocrat gets the keys.

articles.title: Iran cybersnoops still LARPing as ransomware crooks in espionage ops
articles.summary: One in eight employees would sell their work credentials like they're hawking concert tickets, with 13% admitting they've already cashed in. Cybersecurity's biggest threat remains the human willingness to monetize access for pizza money.

articles.title: The Hacker News Launches 'Cybersecurity Stars Awards 2026' — Submissions Now Open
articles.summary: Iranian state hackers MuddyWater pulled a perfect false flag op, using Microsoft Teams to steal creds while cosplaying as ransomware gangs. Because nothing says 'legitimate business meeting' like credential harvesting through corporate chat apps.

articles.title: Windows Phone Link Exploited by CloudZ RAT to Steal Credentials and OTPs
articles.summary: Google launches Binary Transparency for Android to prove their apps aren't backdoored supply chain nightmares. Finally, a public ledger that actually serves the public instead of just enriching crypto bros.

articles.title: Why airlines are always going bankrupt
articles.summary: CloudZ RAT weaponized Windows Phone Link to steal OTPs and credentials, turning your convenient PC-phone bridge into a highway for hackers. Microsoft's 'seamless integration' strikes again.

articles.title: 15-year-old detained over massive data breach at French government agency
articles.summary: 2026 crowned the year of AI-assisted attacks after a 17-year-old in Osaka used malicious code to breach 7 million Kaikatsu Club records. Gen Z proving they don't need decades of experience to pull off massive data heists.

articles.title: Your work apps are quietly handing 19 data points to someone
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly breached France Titres and put 12-18 million government records up for sale like they're flipping Pokemon cards. French bureaucracy meets teenage entrepreneurship in the most dystopian way possible.

articles.title: Attackers are cashing in on fresh 'CopyFail' Linux flaw
articles.summary: Your favorite work apps are quietly sharing 19 data points about you to unknown third parties, because apparently corporate surveillance is just a feature now. Gmail, Teams, and Zoom turning your productivity into their profit.
